This is probably my favourite game. The levels get progressively more challenging but never feel frustrating (to me at least), with the exception of the last two bonus levels that both cost me multiple hours. I have heard some people had to look up where to find the hidden tetrahedrons, though in my experience they were rather easy to spot (I don't know if it is different in hard mode). The gameplay mostly comes down to timing your moves right. I took my time so my playtime at time of review is exactly one playthrough for someone who doesn't play games like this very often. The sounds and visuals are great and there is a small storyline for a tiny bit of context. 

During my playthrough, I've encountered only few bugs, none of which are gamebreaking:
- In one level (I think it was somewhere in world two) the game would sometimes have lags where everything would slow down for a second or two.
- In world 5, I've noticed that the hearts display sometimes shows a lesser amount of hearts and lives than I actually had.
- In the finale, retrying the level or exiting to the world map after a loss both crash the game. It's not that bad though, the progress up until that point is saved.

Octahedron would be great for speedrunners. It has medals for completing each level under certain amounts of time or using only up to a certain amounts of platforms. As a casual player, I have to admit these challenges look too difficult for me, at least after the first few levels.
 
Overall I'd definitely recommend!

Visually, this game looks very unique among it's peers and thus stands out from the other, boasting a very "funky" aesthetic, and also comes with a fun soundtrack by Chipzel that fits very well the artistic direction.

It somehow manages to almost always offer 1 new gameplay element per level, each level felt different from the others, and they were challenging and quite a blast to play through !

There are a few minor issues, such as the platform sometime being a little too high to feel comfortable to land on them from under (Actually, "climbing up" by creating multiple platform and jumping straight up felt weird in general : might have to do with how short the jumping height is compared to the distance you would have to travel upward in some cases), or how a few amount of introduced gameplay element's mechanic were hard to decipher.
but it's main issue is that the visual effect are so saturated, you would sometime find yourself getting hurt because you couldn't see the threat coming (this is especially true for the few last levels )

But otherwise, I had good time playing it and I don't think I would see a game that has a similar vibe for a while !

옥타히드론! 재미있게 플레이한 게임입니다.
각 스테이지마다 정해진 개수의 발판을 만들어 가면서 수집할 거리들을 모으고 끝부분에 도달하는 방식으로 이루어져 있습니다. 퍼즐 요소가 들어있기도 하고, 게임 내 사물들이 배경 음악에 맞춰 움직이는 걸 보니 개인적으로 꽤 마음에 들었어요.
배경 음악은 이 게임의 개발자와 슈퍼 헥사곤의 배경 음악을 만든 Chipzel을 포함해 네 사람이 주로 만들었는데(엔딩 삽입곡 제외), 게임을 하면서 들으니 정말 좋았습니다. 한 곡도 빠짐없이 다 마음에 들었습니다.
난이도는 초중반에는 진행에 문제가 전혀 없을 정도로 무난하지만, [spoiler]월드 4 중반부터 월드 5까지[/spoiler]의 구간은 짧지만 상당히 어려워서 애를 먹을 수 있습니다. 이 부분 때문에 중간에 이 게임을 그만두기도 했어요.
또 각 레벨마다 특정 조건을 충족해야 얻을 수 있는 (타임 어택, 발판 수 제한, 노 데스 등) 메달들이 있는데, 다 수집하는 건... 그냥 안 하시는 게 낫습니다.
다소 두서없이 리뷰를 쓰기는 했지만, 제 생각에는 이 게임을 할지 말지 데모를 직접 플레이하시고 판단해보시는 게 제일 좋겠습니다.

So, I played this game way back in 2019 on the Nintendo Switch.  Absolutely loved it.  Fast forward to November 2024, when I awakened last night around 11:30, could not sleep afterwards so I began perusing through my enormous backlog and Octahedron came into view.  With some trepidation (because I remember how this was a very precise and sometimes twitch platformer), I launched the game and played through the entirety of the first world.  All the feelings I had in 2019, were accurate.  The aesthetic, the controls, the platforming, the music, the level design, all sublime.  I cannot comprehend how this game did not get more recognition while under license from “Square Enix” who did, let me remember, umm, zero marketing for this game.  It should be noted that the developer, “Demimonde” is highly talented and created one of my favorite platformers of all time, definitely in my top ten.  This game comes highly, highly recommended.  -9.5/10-LoA-

"Octahedron" stands as a testament to the incredible talent of Monomirror, who single-handedly crafted this vibrant and bombastic world. As a self-taught game designer, he has not only set a high bar but also redefined what one person can achieve in game development. Everything from the coding and art to the enemies, lighting, and level design is meticulously and impressively crafted.

In my experience, and as someone with high standards when it comes to platformers, "Octahedron" effortlessly joins the ranks of my all-time favorites, standing shoulder to shoulder with games like "Mega Man 9," "Shovel Knight," and "Hollow Knight." Its level design is nothing short of impressive, arguably the best since "Mega Man 9." This creative prowess extends to its soundtrack and overall presentation, contributing to a supremely fun gaming experience.

What truly sets "Octahedron" apart is its holistic and unified approach in its design and aesthetics. Each level and mechanic is thoughtfully constructed, offering a gameplay experience that's both challenging and satisfying. The game not only meets but exceeds the expectations of platformer enthusiasts, earning its place as my Game of the Year (2018) and my favorite platformer of this generation.

"Octahedron" is a game you don't want to miss. Its seamless blend of innovative design, captivating music, and engaging gameplay mechanics makes it a remarkable journey. For anyone who appreciates well-crafted platformers, "Octahedron" delivers an experience that’s both refreshing and nostalgically familiar, and it does so flawlessly. My rating is a resounding 10/10.

Fun precision platformer with a cool "platforming" gimmick.  Level design and gameplay is tightly focused and the presentation matches in quality.  Felt like everything tied together real well that I started to enjoy the novelty of peering into how this strange neon world worked a little further in with each new creature/obstacle introduced.

Wishing there was a neutral option, but leaning more towards not liking this game than liking it, so not recommended will have to do.

Octahedron, has an interesting mechanic where you can create temporary platforms under your character in order to traverse its levels. This builds into the platforming puzzles.

[h1]What I don't like about Octahedron:[/h1]
[list]
[*]Any given screen is a mess to look at. It is colourful and retro, but not very practical.
[*]First time playing through levels, it is difficult to understand what can and can't kill you. That's fine, trial and error isn't unusual for platformers however this is yet another visual design choice flaw, and you can end up confusing yourself as you progress and more mechanics are introduced
[*]The default keyboard controls are terrible, if you plan to play this make sure to change them. "Control" for jump instead of "space"? "Y" is to change platform type along with "X", have the developers never seen a keyboard before?
[*]Speaking of controls, this character controls poorly, feels sluggish to balance the platform mechanic, and sometimes platforms are created slightly below the character, which doesn't seem like an issue until you try to create a platform and quickly jump, thus not being able to jump due to not being on a surface (this is hell for least time challenges)
[*]Challenges are not too difficult, but the least time challenges are hell. If you want to complete those, good luck, as they are are beyond unbalanced, you must play perfectly, no room for error at all. You will frequently find yourself failing by a few seconds because of this.
[/list]

[h1]What I like about Octahedron:[/h1]
The only thing I can say I like is that the gameplay is somewhat interesting, but that's about it... I boot up this game every once in a while, with the intent of getting all the achievements, because that appears to be the most enjoyment I am getting out of this.

[h1]Neutral points[/h1]
[list]
[*]Music is meh, nothing stellar and nothing I haven't heard before. It's bordering on generic.
[*]There isn't really a story, a man is sucked into a strange world, and is trying to progress (honestly the intro is so forgettable, that I sometimes forget that it even happened). So you just kind of progress through the levels, and the only real motivation is just to challenge yourself.
[/list]

Overall a 5/10, it's not terrible or unplayable, but it could be better. I may have got it on sale, but the full price is hard to justify.

Sinceramente no entiendo como este juego pudo pasar tan desapercibido, al menos en Steam.
Yo me enteré de su existencia cuando anunciaron la Transfixed edition para Nintendo Swtich, y desde entonces siempre me dejé como tarea probar el juego y ver que tal.
Lo que me llamó la atención en ese momento fue ver los artistas que componen la banda sonora, principalmente el hecho de que Chipzel haya participado en esto (si un juego tiene soundtrack suyo, automáticamente lo hace bueno xd) así que guiándome por esa lógica estúpida me lo compré en oferta hace relativamente poco.

Es uno de los mejores juegos de plataformas que probé (sin sarcasmo esta vez lmao), fácil de aprender pero complicado de dominar si no te acostumbras a jugarlo seguido. Los controles se pueden configurar a gusto, los que trae son medios raros pero sirven.
La dificultad está super bien puesta, no es como esos juegos plataformeros que se "fuerzan" a ser infernalmente difíciles y así ganar algo de notoriedad, acá la cosa progresa según vas avanzando. Durante los primeros mundos, la dificultad es una papa pero eso va cambiando conforme sigas completando niveles... Ojo, todo sin exagerar con cosas complicadas. Como mucho, el juego te puede poner algunos objetos rodeados de 100000 obstáculos, pero completar el nivel en el que estás siempre es relativamente fácil si prestas atención al entorno y no vas a lo loco. De hecho, si también eso se te dificulta, puedes cambiar a dificultad fácil en cualquier instancia del juego, pero esto imposibilita volver a seleccionar la dificultad NORMAL en esa partida.
Gráficamente hablando, obviamente no ofrece gráficos en 4k de la vida real, es un bendito juego de plataformas en 2d, pero si posee como punto fuerte el hecho de tener una iluminación preciosa y fondos psicodélicos, el cual va cambiando según avances en el nivel o recojas objetos. Flashero a más no poder si no le bajas un poco los gráficos y las opciones de los efectos, pero no te lo recomiendo por que es uno de los principales encantos del juego por así decirlo.
(Jugar esta cosa bajo los efectos de las drogas debe ser una experiencia única xd)

Como dije antes, cuenta con una banda sonora en la que participó Chipzel, pero algo que me sorprendió es que casi TODAS las demás canciones superan las suyas, es un soundtrack precioso y que queda genial puesto dentro del juego. Yo cometí el error de jugarlo sin sonido las primeras veces, así que cuando descubrí la música y los soniditos que tenía quedé fuera de este mundo amiwos míos. 😢
Super recomendado que lo compres en la edición coleccionista, así puedas disfrutar de todas las canciones tranquilamente. Por las dudas, también tiene una página en Bandcamp donde la banda sonora está disponible pero no se si a un precio menor o mayor al de Steam.

Lo de la jugabilidad es seguramente la parte más confusa del juego pero a la vez la más satisfactoria:
Al inicio del juego te explican que te vas a tener que manejar desplegando plataformas para poder subir en el nivel, pasa que dichas plataformas desaparecen a los pocos segundos de colocarlas, y encima dependiendo del nivel en el que estés, puedes poner más o menos plataformas en el escenario, así que eso complica muchísimo las cosas de vez en cuando. ¿Entonces por que carajo digo lo de que esto es una característica satisfactoria? Bueno, al completar cada mundo, se nos desbloquea un tipo de plataforma nueva, con una función MUY específica, que si bien en niveles nuevos puede llegar a complicar muchísimo el gameplay por la cantidad de veces que vas a tener que rotar entre una y otra, cuando juegas mundos viejos con plataformas nuevas, llegas a descubrir secretos y objetos que con una anterior no hubieras podido, y esto es lo que le añade gran parte de la re-jugabilidad a este juego, el resto es gracias a los logros de medallas que trae. En todo lo que llevo jugando no me topé ni un bug ni error respecto a esto, 0 problemas.

Si te gustan los juegos de plataformas esta delicia no puede faltar en tu biblioteca, el precio normal que tiene vale totalmente la pena y más todavía si lo encuentras en oferta (con el simple hecho de ver los gifs en la página de la tienda te das cuenta de la hermosura que es), y bueno, si no te convence nada de esto, ni los trailers, el juego tiene una opción de Demo en la que vas a ver bastante bien de que trata...

Things I Disliked: 
Lack of diversity visually and maybe a bit too much going on visually in general.
Game would have heavily benefited from doing even just a simple hue shift to differentiate between the different sets of levels. Every level in the game has the exact same visual style with no exceptions. It's not bad as it is, I just would have preferred some more visual diversity.

Trying to rapidly create and jump off of platforms is a bit.......less than ideal IMO. You can for sure get used to it, it just requires that you make sure you only create the platform at either the very top of your jump or as you are falling, otherwise your character will kind of "skip" slightly and wont jump because you were slightly above the platform. This gives the impression of the game not registering your input sometimes.
It adds to the skill required, but personally I would just prefer if creating a platform just immediately stopped your vertical movement and/or anchored you to the platform instantly.

This game started out very promising, but by the third level you can already see what this game devolves into - precision platforming without the controls to back it up. My favourite!

The premise of Octahedron is that you control your neon character through a visually appealing world, with blinking backgrounds fitting to the beat and plenty of stuff to collect. The gimmick is that you can summon platforms to appear under you to reach higher areas; you can also surf on those platforms for a short time before they disappear.

Now the problem is: this game has several medals you can earn for each level; one for collecting everything, one for only using a certain amount of platforms, one for completing it under a specific amount of time and so on. Especially the time medals are very frustrating to get with the controls of this game. If you just summon a platform under you while jumping, instead of just immediately being glued to that platform and able to jump (which would make the controls 100 % better), you are still stuck in the air for the fraction of a second before landing on said platform. It makes precision jumping a nightmare because you have to factor in the delay of you being in the air before your feet land on the platform, and with the amount of platforms you have to summon in quick succession, you are bound to mess up somewhere; especially considering you HAVE to do everything perfectly to even have a chance at the time medals.

The visuals of the game are also waaaay overblown. By the third level, there are already so many obstacles on the screen that are out to hurt you that mesh with the blinking background and the overbearing amount of visual effects - it is very hard to follow what is going on.

Long story short, the amount of patience needed for this game is just not for me. Everything visually meshes with each other in the worst way, and the platforming is clunky and delayed. Maybe it gets better later on, but I did not get past the third level.

Octahedron is another Concept Platformer, and its concept is this: what if you could hit a button to spawn a platform under your feet? It pulls hours of great vertically-scrolling platforming from that premise with constantly inventive mechanics and level design. Levels are constantly introducing fun new elements like platforms that toggle solidity each time you spawn a platform, or enemies that try to jump you from below, pushing the platform you're on to the ceiling. Each level feels distinct and is built for replay, with medals available for beating a level with all collectibles, without dying, below a par time, and below par platform spawns. Reaching the end of Octahedron is within the grasp of any platformer fan, and the medals are a wonderful extra challenge for dedicated players. Meeting platform pars is especially fun, asking you to work out the most efficient paths through each level.

My biggest complaint with Octahedron has to do with the final challenge. The lead-up to the end is a lot of fun, handing you a power-up you've been wanting since the start of the game and giving you a gauntlet of fast-paced levels to use it. But the very last level changes up the formula for the worse. Without going into spoilers, I'll just say that while it's not too difficult, I believe it's too chaotic. It's just not as interesting as all the carefully-crafted level design up to that point. But while that's a disappointment to end on, it's a small part of the game.

The game encourages multiple playthroughs of each level, and each time you will be approaching the level differently to earn different medals for fast completion, collecting 100% of the items in the level, and efficient platforming.

Octahedron is never boring. It's constantly evolving how you play the game through clever level design and upgrading of your platform, but it also never gets too complicated. It remains, from start to finish, a game about timing your jumps and platforms to get to the end of the level, and never loses its way. The soundtrack is absolutely incredible, and is almost worth the price on its own. I would highly recommend buying the collectors edition if you enjoy electronica/synth/chiptune type music.

Any issues I have with the game are so unbelievably minor that they're almost not worth mentioning. The game can also, at times, strain your hands on some of the longer levels that require constant jumping/platforming, depending on how you're playing (on keyboard, in my case). It's very rare that this happens though, as most levels don't take longer than 2-4 minutes on average.

점프 도중에 공중에 발판을 생성할 수 있으며, 생성한 발판 이외의 땅에 닿기 전까지 사용할 수 있는 발판의 수가 매 스테이지마다 다르다. 발판에 올라탄 채로 이동과 점프 또한 할 수 있지만, 발판은 일정 시간이 지나면 사라져 버린다. 맵에 있는 탈출구에 도달하면 클리어. 발판으로 전구를 부수면 다이아몬드를 가진 꽃이 생성되며, 각 단계마다 이 다이아몬드를 일정량 이상 취득해야 다음 단계가 개방된다.

난이도는 '일반(Normal)'과 '쉬움(Easy)'이 있으며, 쉬움 난이도는 받는 피해가 절반(하트 1/2개)으로 감소하기 때문에 쉬운 플레이가 가능하다. 처음부터 쉬움으로 시작할 수도 있고 보통으로 시작했더라도 쉬움으로 바꿀 수 있으나, 한번 쉬움으로 바꾼 난이도를 보통으로 되돌릴 수는 없다.

단순 클리어는 비교적 쉬운 편이나(5단계는 예외로 상당히 어렵다), 각 맵에 마련된 '메달'을 취득하려면 상당한 난관이 기다리고 있다. 메달은 다음이 있으며, 클리어 화면에서 확인할 수 있다:

- 100% = 스테이지에 흩어져 있는 30개의 다이아몬드(◆)와 8개의 정사면체(▲)를 모두 모으고 클리어 시 획득.
- Par any% = 수집 요소를 얼마나 모았는지와는 상관 없이, 지정된 수 이하의 발판만을 사용하여 클리어 시 획득.
- Par 100% = 수집 요소를 모두 모으면서 지정된 수 이하의 발판만을 사용하여 클리어 시 획득. 당연히 Par any%보다는 발판 수 제한이 많지만, 결코 any%보다 쉽다는 의미가 아니다.
- Deus = 한 번도 죽지 않고 클리어 시 획득. 만약 단 한번의 피격도 없었다면 대신 Deus ♥ 메달을 얻는다.
- Time = 지정된 제한 시간 두 개중 긴 시간 안에 들어오면 획득. 만약 짧은 시간 안에 들어왔다면 대신 Time + 메달을 얻는다.

The level design here doesn't predictably add more stuff and gets harder, but plays around with different concepts and ways to go around a level. For example, generally you are given a couple of platforms to create in each level, for example 2 to 4 until you touch ground, but in one level you are given 50 platforms because there is only a couple of solid platforms to stand on. This is just one example of many.

Quizá sea muy poco objetivo de mi parte empezar este "análisis" con la siguiente declaración, pero: me basto la demo para saber que Octahedron es uno de los mejores juegos de plataformas que he jugado en mi vida. 

La meta del juego es ir yendo de plataforma en plataforma para llegar al final de cada nivel, para lograr esto contamos con un salto que variará en la medida que dejemos presionado el botón de salto (mientras más tiempo lo dejemos presionado, más alto saltará nuestro personaje) pero el problema está en que las plataformas en general son muy altas para nuestro simple salto; es ahí donde surge el principal atractivo jugable de octahedron: la habilidad de crear plataformas. Cada que saltemos, tendremos la oportunidad de crear plataformas presionando nuevamente el botón de salto, estas nuevas plataformas tienen varias características: para empezar, igual que el salto, estas duran más si dejamos presionado el botón de salto, pero además tienen la particularidad de que se pueden mover cuando nosotros lo hacemos, es decir, creamos una plataforma y, manteniendo pulsado el botón de salto, nos movemos, y la plataforma lo hace con nosotros (es más sencillo de lo que parece). Además, la plataforma ira siendo cada vez más poderosa conforme vayamos avanzando en el juego, pasando de ser una simple plataforma más, a un arma mortífera que te será de mucha utilidad en los niveles más avanzados

Cada nivel nos muestra la cantidad límite de plataformas que podemos crear en él, en algunos niveles serán dos, en otras 5 etc., y el número de plataformas que podemos realizar se reinicia al tocar el piso, es decir, supongamos que podemos crear 5 plataformas y las vamos creando, el juego nos muestra cuantas plataformas más podemos crear hasta que se nos agoten; sin embargo, si tocamos algún tipo de tierra este contador se reinicia. Es esta limitación de creación de plataformas, junto a los obstáculos y enemigos, lo que constituye el principal desafío de los niveles.

Y hablando de los niveles: estos son fantásticos. Le sacan provecho al mundo (uno muy  bonito, lleno de colores neón) y a las mecánicas jugables. A excepción de unos cuantos, los niveles se sienten únicos y expresivos, va a pasar un buen rato hasta que empieces a ver repetición en los obstáculos, y, aun así, el juego se las ingenia para sorprenderte hasta el final. Imanes que atraen a las plataformas que creas o enemigos que se comen tus plataformas creadas, son solo algunos de los distintos y muy variados retos que el juego te pone. Dichos retos, por cierto, son bastante desafiantes a ratos, el juego no teme probar tu habilidad en ciertos momentos, aunque sin hacerte sufrir mucho, creo la dificultad está muy bien balanceada: el juego te da las herramientas necesarias para pasarlo (siendo generoso en muchas ocasiones) pero te reta cada que puede, todo fallo es tuyo y eso es muy bueno (además, al acabarlo por primera vez se liberan nuevas dificultades). 

Quizá mi única queja con los niveles es que hay muchos focos, me explico: cada nivel tiene una cantidad de focos que debemos romper con ayuda de nuestras plataformas y obtener unas flores que salen de ellos, mismas que son necesarias para desbloquear nuevos mundos, no es que este mal, pero al ser demasiados te distraes mucho del objetivo principal y por tanto se pierde un poco del dinamismo del juego. Es una queja menor que realmente no afecta al juego, pero me parece pertinente decirlo sobre todo porque el juego te reta a sacar el 100% en cada nivel y para lograr ese 100%, necesitas pasar cada nivel obteniendo todos los coleccionables, no muriendo y usando una determinada cantidad de plataformas. La rejugabilidad está asegurada gracias a esto, pero se siente un poco cansado a la larga. En su defensa diré que te permite hacerlo cuantas veces quieras y de nuevo, casi todos los niveles son tan buenos que valen la pena jugarlos varias veces, pero si creo que un poco menos de esto, en algunos niveles, ayudaría al juego.

También en cada nivel hay unos pequeños octaedros que están por todo el mapa, también son coleccionables necesarios para el 100%, pero estos me gustan mucho más porque obtenerlos representan un reto en sí mismo ya que están en lugares de difícil acceso o muchas veces escondidas en algún lado, y además ayudan a desbloquear niveles opcionales que te dan recompensas al pasarlos.  

Mención aparte merece el nivel final, el cual me gustó mucho, y me parece un clímax adecuado que brinda satisfacción al terminarlo.

También menciono la música (la cual es muy buena), ya que, como la propia página de steam resalta, cuenta con la participación de varias personas, entre ellas Chipzel (Super Hexagon). Me gusta mucho su trabajo y de hecho mis canciones favoritas del juego son las que ella hizo, en sí todo el ost es de música electrónica o similares, no soy fan de este tipo de música, pero aquí queda muy bien y me parece muy buena siendo tonadas pegajosas que van acorde a la estética y ritmo de juego. Además, como igualmente señala la página de steam, los enemigos y obstáculos se mueven al ritmo de las canciones, lo cual es cierto y da cierta importancia a las canciones (ser más que mera compañía), pero debo señalar que no me parece que TODOS los enemigos y obstáculos lo hagan, no sé si fue mi percepción la que está mal, pero aparte de un par de enemigos y obstáculos, la mayoría se movía diferente al ritmo de la música. De nuevo: igual y soy yo quien está mal, la verdad ahí sí no puedo decir, pero independientemente de eso, casi todos los enemigos tienen patrones muy reconocibles y sencillos de aprender.

En conclusión: Octahedron me encantó. Me parece un gran juego que adopta una mecánica muy interesante y le saca todo el provecho, desde el primer momento y hasta el último, el juego te desafía y brinda una gran satisfacción al completar los niveles, acompañado de un buen ost y varios secretos. Lo recomiendo ampliamente a cualquier persona, especialmente a aquellos que disfruten los buenos juegos de plataformas.

Well this game is bloody amazing.
Wish I knew it was out sooner, This is truly a hidden gem on Steam.

You use a basic mechanic of creating platforms that stay underneath you as long as you hold the button down.
You can walk, and the platform moves with you. But only for a short time.

You are usually given 1 or 2 that you can create after a jump ( the levels show you how many platforms you can make in mid-air)

That's just the basic, though.
There are several different types of plarforms you earn as you complete entire stages, there's a meter needing 130 crystals, once you earn them - and beat all the levels in that stage - you can unlock a new platform, and move on to the next set of levels.

They add layers into the basic mechanic that really make you think.
Also, you collect little triangles, they usually pose a puzzle challenge in how to get them- and get away without taking damage , because if you get hit after grabbing one, it resets.

There's also lightbulbs, you "surf" your platforms through, breaking them ; which causes flowers to appear higher up in the level. That is what you need to collect in order to advance.

You can take 3 hits ( or more, depending on powerups, etc ) 
When you take a hit, you are sent back to the furthest checkpoint in the stage ( even if you backtrack to the bottom, and then get hit - you are sent to the last checkpoint you reached progression-wise.)

When you exhaust all your hearts, you are sent back to thestart  of the level, and lose a life - but the level remains , all the stuff you did in it is still done , you're just missing a life, and have to re-climb up.

The visual style is simplyamazing, it's very colorful, neon, very fun to look at it all unfolding.

Absolutely recommend this to game, it is simply a gem.

Puzzle platformer might be one of the most saturated game genres out there and it might often feel like every conceivable idea or gimmick has already been explored. However, Octahedron's core special mechanic of making your own platforms out of thin air is simply genius. The level design itself is amazing, with most levels truly having their own identity, but even beyond that there's a huge difference in playstyle between a level which allows you one platform or fifty of them, elevating the variety and fun when going from level to level much higher than is usual for games of this genre.

Most of the game had just the right difficulty level for me, difficult enough to be enjoyable but not too hard to feel like you're constantly hitting brick walls and getting frustrated (although 5-Δ is a real difficulty spike). I also really liked that if you're observant enough you can spot the secret areas. The final area is a bit weird (and surprisingly easy) and the final boss is a bit finger-numbing, but overall Octahedron has quickly replaced Super Meat Boy as my favourite platformer ever.

OCTAHEDRON is simply pure bliss from start to finish for anyone who's a fan of challenging platformers. With its punchy neon aesthetics and fantastic soundtrack, once you're past the short, intuitive tutorial you're straight into the meat of the game with no hand-holding necessary. There are some unobtrusive story cutscenes at the start and end of the game, however everything in between can be played through with no barriers, or any text to read.

Practically every level has a unique mechanic that never gets exhausted, with new enemies, obstacles and platforms that are introduced and swiftly subverted, not to mention the surfing platforms you create yourself which give a great sense of freedom. Collectibles of varying difficulty are strewn across the level but rarely feel like a slog, particularly due to careful level design that allows you to backtrack and collect everything in one sitting regardless of later upgrades. They rarely gate progress, and the harder items simply unlock bonus levels that aren't required to beat the game, thus allow for some extra challenge. Not to mention the medals for completing levels in as few platforms as possible, or with no deaths.

The art-style works perfectly with the type of arcade-like platformer this is, and despite remaining the same throughout, never got tedious. Some people may find the noise distracting (there are options to dull the effects in the menu) however it never felt like it was getting in the way of gameplay. As for the soundtrack, and the way the game's rhythm flows with it (without being a necessity to play along with the rhythm), I have nothing but praise. I'll be listening to it non-stop.

If I had to point out anything, I guess it would be accessibility for people who may want to experience the soundtrack and art, but could find the later stages quite difficult. You can take 3 hits before respawning at a nearby checkpoint, and have 4 tries until having to restart over. Personally I feel this is pretty fair and individual levels don't tend to last too long. But maybe a mode with no life limit (like how some still genuinely challenging platformers work, i.e VVVVVV or Super Meat Boy) could be useful without drastically changing the nature of the game.

If Steam had scores, and for people who love numbers, I'd give this a solid 9/10. I very much feel I got my money's worth with an initial 10 hour playthrough, and 20+ hours of trying harder modes, beating par goals, and going fast. Buy this game now.
